LESSON: ANIMALS. • CHARACTERISTICS OF ANIMALS AS LIVING THINGS. • VERTEBRATES AND INVERTEBRATES.

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Living things and their Environment
Topic 1.2: Animals. • Characteristics of animals as living things. • Vertebrates and invertebrates.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Animals. • Characteristics of animals as living things. • Vertebrates and invertebrates., part of Living things and their Environment in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: How are animals different from each other? 2. Why are animals considered as living things?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Animals. • Characteristics of animals as living things. • Vertebrates and invertebrates. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner develops signing skills by participating actively in discussions about the main differences between

vertebrates and invertebrates.

• Creativity and Imagination: Observation skill is enhanced as the learner discovers new ways of doing things by observing how other learners are

developing a portfolio of vertebrates and invertebrates using magazine cut outs.

• Learning to learn: The learner develops relationships as they collaboratively use print and captioned non-print media to search for information on

characteristics of animals.

8

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner shows diligence as they engage in roles and duties assigned by the teacher when making a portfolio of vertebrates and

invertebrates.

• Respect: The learner demonstrates humility by appreciating divergent ideas from peers as they discuss the main differences between vertebrates

and invertebrates.

PCIs:

Safety and security: personal safety and security skills are developed as the learner observes safety when handling animals.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The information on characteristics of animals as living things is linked to the study of livestock in Agriculture and Nutrition.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Charts

● Cameras

● Print and non-print media

● Flowers,
